population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 46.5M of ~267M US adults are currently on an incretin for any indication (17.4%). Age check: 0.20×8 + 0.33×15.5 + 0.24×27.2 + 0.23×18 = 1.6 + 5.1 + 6.5 + 4.1 ≈ 17.4. Income thirds 22/16.5/13.5 average 17.3. The bottom third rose (12→13.5) on Medicaid expansion despite losing gray-market supply. The middle fell (18→16.5) on cash price rises and the import crackdown. The top slipped (23→22) on employer retreat and on NAION- and scandal-driven stops. The 65+ band rose (14.5→18) on the Continuity Model expansion. Payer mix of the 46.5M: diabetes- or cardiac-coded 21.2M (Medicare Part D 9.5M, Medicaid 2.5M, commercial/other 9.2M); employer obesity coverage 6.0M; Medicare Continuity obesity-only 3.8M; Medicaid obesity-only 3.5M; brand cash via TrumpRx/direct 8.5M; gray market 3.5M. Sum 46.5M. Public programmes pay for 9.5 + 2.5 + 3.8 + 3.5 = 19.3M (41.5%), more than commercial insurance (15.2M, 32.7%), cash (18%) or gray market (7.5%). About 4M current users are on retatrutide, spread across those categories. Cycling arithmetic: ever 26% − current 17.4% = 8.6 pp (~23M adults) used and are off now. Restart dynamics as in the parent, plus Medicare/Medicaid re-enrolment, make ~40% of current users restarters (0.40×17.4 ≈ 7.0 pp). About 22% of those currently off had already cycled once (0.22×8.6 ≈ 1.9 pp). (7.0 + 1.9)/26 ≈ 34% of ever-users have stopped and restarted at least once. Of the ~23M off-drug ever-users, about 8M stopped because of coverage or price, including ~2.5M former gray-market users cut off by the 2029 tariff and import enforcement. About 1M are formally locked out of Medicare or Medicaid after an adherence lapse, and ~1.5M say they stopped over the NAION warning or the Novo documents. Never-users include ~30M adults with obesity who were never able to afford or access the drug. Pediatric: ~0.6% of ~73M under-18s (~0.44M), down from 0.7% because nine states restricted prescribing to minors; use remains concentrated in high-income zip codes and in states without restrictions. Roughly one in four US children lives in a household where an adult is on the drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: from Jan 2030 the CMMI GLP-1 Continuity Model is mandatory for all Part D sponsors. Eligibility widened to BMI ≥30 with one weight-related comorbidity, or BMI ≥35, and retatrutide and both orals are now on the formulary. Terms are unchanged: Medicare pays ~$245/month and the beneficiary copay is ~$50. The adherence conditions remain (≥80% proportion of days covered, ≥5% loss at 6 months). The lockout falls from 12 to 6 months, and lapses for a documented adverse event are exempt. Enrolment is ~3.8M obesity-only beneficiaries by end-2030, up from 1.5M. Spending is 3.8M × $245 × 12 ≈ $11.2B/yr gross federal, with beneficiary copays of 3.8M × $50 × 12 ≈ $2.3B/yr on top. Medicaid: 31 states (up from 19) cover obesity at $245 for ~3.5M enrollees. Gross cost is 3.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $10.3B/yr, of which the federal share at a ~65% blended FMAP is ≈ $6.7B. Fifteen states attach adherence waivers. Counting diabetes-coded use, public programmes are now the largest payer of incretin fills (~41.5%).
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ generic semaglutide brands at ~$8–40/month, and generic oral semaglutide is available there since 2028. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and most of Southeast Asia have injectable generics; Canada's sell at CAD 70–110. Indian exporters are hit by the US Section 232 peptide tariff and the import crackdown, and are redirecting volume to the Gulf, Africa and Latin America. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: Price follows a shock-up path. The Jun 2029 Section 232 tariff (50% on imported GLP-1 peptide API and finished injectables from countries without an onshoring agreement, chiefly India and China), together with FDA/CBP ending enforcement discretion on personal importation of incretins, pushed gray-market import prices from $60–120 to $110–220/month. Seizures made supply unreliable, and gray-market users fell from ~6M to ~3.5M. Brand cash prices rose: TrumpRx injectable semaglutide went from $199 to $249 (Jan 2030), Zepbound from $249–299 to $299–349, and retatrutide direct cash from $399 to $449. Lilly and Novo cited tariff exposure on part of their API supply and onshoring capex. The oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) stayed at $149 under the TrumpRx deal, so new starts are now ~45% oral. List prices are unchanged (Wegovy $1,349). Employer weight-management coverage fell 44% → 38% (Business Group on Health 2030). Most remaining plans require a comorbidity code or a vendor programme, and the 30–49 age band, which depends most on employer plans, fell accordingly. 503A 'personalised' compounding survives at the margin. Research-peptide retatrutide persists in gym communities at $200–300, now shipped through domestic relabellers.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly; approved Feb 2028, broad rollout 2029–30)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, Sep 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers
alcohol reduction: phase 3 AUD trial positive on heavy-drinking days (Oct 2029); sNDA filed Mar 2030, decision expected 2031; widely prescribed off-label in the meantime
research-peptide retatrutide in gym and 'recomposition' communities
microdosing for 'metabolic health', diminished since the import crackdown
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care, now barred in nine states
drugs.pipeline_note: No new indication was approved this step. The 'surgical-grade loss from a pen' driver is realised as retatrutide's broad rollout rather than a new launch. Lilly's autoinjector scale-up ended allocation limits in mid-2029. Medicare added retatrutide to the Continuity Model at the $245 rate in Jan 2030, and ~4M Americans are on it by end-2030. Two-year extension data hold ~28–29% mean loss, with ~30% in BMI ≥35. US bariatric surgery volumes are ~30% below 2026. Survodutide was filed in 2029 and is under FDA review, with a decision expected 2031. Amycretin was filed in late 2029 and could not be approved before late 2030; it is under review. MariTide (monthly) read out phase 3 in 2030 and has not been filed. The semaglutide AUD sNDA is pending. The FDA cited the ongoing semaglutide pharmacovigilance inquiry when it declined priority review. The global incretin market is ~$125B (2030): volume is flat in the US and growing ex-US, US unit prices are slightly higher, and Lilly holds ~60% of US new starts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading side-effect cause of discontinuation. Worst at retatrutide's top doses and with unsupervised research-peptide titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss. Retatrutide real-world cholecystectomy rates are about 1.5× tirzepatide's in early claims data.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. MDL ongoing, first bellwether trials scheduled 2031, now alongside NAION claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concern sharpened by ~4M on retatrutide and by the Continuity expansion bringing in more adults over 65. Cohorts continue to associate long-term use in women over 60 with lower bone density, and a hip-fracture signal is under study.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label recommends resistance exercise and protein counselling. The Continuity Model covers one annual DEXA scan for enrollees 65+; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Pooled reanalysis of trial data with ophthalmic adjudication, together with Sentinel and Nordic registries, supports a roughly 2-fold relative risk. Absolute excess is about 1–2 cases per 10,000 person-years, higher in people with diabetes, small optic discs and sleep apnea. Unsealed MDL documents showed Novo deferred an internally proposed adjudicated NAION analysis in 2024–25.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class Warning & Precaution (Nov 2029) across all GLP-1 receptor agonist products, including the orals, tirzepatide and retatrutide. It advises urgent ophthalmic evaluation for sudden vision loss, discontinuation if NAION is confirmed, and caution in patients with prior NAION. The EMA upgraded its label from 'very rare' to a class warning. There is no boxed warning.
Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still unquantified in any registry or label. In 2030 HHS, at the urging of the MAHA wing, funded the first prospective NIH study with a validated anhedonia scale (SHAPS) as a primary endpoint, n≈3,000, reporting 2032. Mainstream societies called the study's origin political. The AUD trial reported 'reduced craving' as efficacy and did not report hedonic tone.
About half of lost weight returns within a year. The 2029 import crackdown produced a natural experiment, with ~2.5M abrupt gray-market stops, now being studied.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Continues to underpin the adherence conditions. Medicare's lockout was cut to 6 months, with exemptions for adverse events.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case series on B12, iron and thiamine at retatrutide-level intake reduction.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional societies recommend baseline and annual labs, which the Continuity Model covers.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The Sentinel cycling study's interim analysis (2030) finds no excess cardiovascular events with cycling. It does suggest a lean-mass 'ratchet': each regain is proportionally more fat. ~34% of ever-users have cycled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; Sentinel study ongoing, final report 2032.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~6,500. Since the crackdown, the share from domestically relabelled research peptides has risen, while reports from imported generics have fallen.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion stands. Personal-importation enforcement discretion for incretins was ended in Jun 2029, with CBP seizures. The research-peptide sites are pursued case by case.

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A US Sentinel analysis (2029) found a weaker association (HR ~1.3) that is still significant after adjusting for diabetes duration. Absolute excess is ~2 per 1,000 person-years beyond year 5.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded (2029) and added hyposmia as a possible adverse reaction, frequency not known, to semaglutide and liraglutide product information. FDA: no label change, review ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mostly mild and dose-related; the second most common reason for stopping retatrutide.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are steady at ~28% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~5–6% from 2026, and sugary drinks ~4–5%. Growth sits in protein, fibre and small-format products. The DTC broadcast-advertising rule ended co-branded 'companion' TV spots, so CPG firms moved to retail-media and pharmacy-app placement. Midwest private-label snack consolidation continues; two more plants closed in Ohio and Indiana.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~3% more over two years, and beer is down ~1–2%. Off-label prescribing to heavy drinkers after the Oct 2029 AUD readout became the industry's most-cited risk. Non-alc keeps growing. In tobacco, the decline in cigarette volumes ran ~1 point faster than trend; Altria cites incretins in guidance.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Half-portion menus are standard, and buffet closures continue. The import crackdown briefly returned some lower-income regainers to value menus, a small 2029–30 tailwind for QSR value chains in the South and Midwest.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue to close stores. Retailers report a two-way churn: retatrutide users moving down three sizes, and crackdown-driven regainers moving back up. Torrid and DXL have shrunk further; neither has failed.

fitness.state: Strength and 'muscle-preservation' studios keep growing, helped by retatrutide labelling and by Medicare Advantage plans covering resistance-training programmes for Continuity enrollees. Big-box cardio gyms are flat. Domestic relabelled research peptides circulate in gym communities.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 38%. Coverage is concentrated on comorbidity codes, and about 1 in 4 large self-funded employers now run BMI or adherence premium differentials. Public programmes are now the largest payer of incretin fills, and Part D sponsors administer the Continuity Model's adherence checks. Bariatric surgery volumes are ~30% below 2026, and hospital bariatric programmes are consolidating.

pharma.state: Lilly is dominant: retatrutide, Foundayo and tirzepatide take ~60% of US new starts. Novo faces the NAION documents, a DOJ civil investigative demand and a Danish FSA inquiry. Its head of global safety departed, and US share is still falling. Revenue grows on ex-US volume and modest US price rises. Indian generic makers lost much of their US gray channel to the tariff.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: In affluent suburbs, thinness after 40 still reads as maintenance, and 'reta face' is a recognised look. A larger body is now read three ways: refusal, a coverage gap, or 'crackdown regain'. People who were visibly losing weight on Indian generics in 2028 and regained in 2029–30 are a recognisable cohort in Ohio and Texas warehouse towns.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers have reshuffled rather than flattened. Medicare and Medicaid now carry older and poorer users at $245, with conditions attached. The squeezed group is the working-age, employer-insured-but-not-covered middle: too well paid for Medicaid, too young for Medicare, now paying $149 for a pill or $249+ for an injection. BMI surcharges still fall mostly on hourly workers at large self-funded employers.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Half portions and protein first are normal in GLP-1 households. Since the NAION warning, an annual eye exam has joined the ritual, and optometry chains advertise 'GLP-1 eye checks'. Church potlucks in Texas and Oklahoma are sites of 'Made Whole' pride. Atlanta's Black church food traditions feature in the 'Bodies Aren't Billing Codes' movement's 2030 'Full Table' Sundays.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On it / off it' is a filter on two major dating apps. Couples split by coverage, one partner on Medicare and the other not yet 65, describe mismatched appetites, around food and otherwise. Low desire is discussed more openly on therapist podcasts and still rarely attributed to the drug in clinic.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is treatable and, at work, increasingly undesirable. Alcohol is now effectively on the list off-label. The backlash has sharpened since the Novo documents: fat-liberation organisers, 'Made Whole' evangelicals and MAHA influencers cite the same scandal to opposite ends. They agree that the companies hid things and that appetite is not a billing code, and on nothing else.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Still unmeasured. The NIH SHAPS study reports in 2032. What is measured is adherence: connected-pen and refill data from ~1 in 4 large self-funded employers' wellness vendors, plus Part D data on 3.8M Continuity enrollees. Vendor white papers correlate adherence with lower absenteeism and turnover, and employers act on the correlation without asking what drives it.
interior_life.framing: Feature and character. Wellness vendors market 'steadiness' and 'regulated workforce' metrics. Managers describe adherent staff as 'even', 'reliable' and 'low-drama'. The drug is framed as treatment for the body, while the steadiness is credited to the person.
interior_life.effect_on_work: At least two national logistics firms and a large hospital system give scheduling priority ('Steady Shift' or 'preferred rostering') to employees enrolled and adherent in the approved weight programme. Formally this is a wellness incentive; in practice it selects for on-drug staff. Because coverage and surcharge waivers follow employment and Continuity requires adherence, adherence and employment now correlate tightly, and causation runs both ways. Sales and hospitality managers still complain about 'flat' closers, though not in writing.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Middle-aged bar trivia, bowling and late-night gaming groups keep thinning. Live music skews to loud, intense, short-format shows. A small Columbus and Detroit 'regain rock' scene of off-drug warehouse workers sings about appetite returning. Stand-up about 'reta face' and 'Steady Shift' is a staple.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Therapists report couples where the on-drug partner feels 'content' and the off-drug partner feels unwanted. A minority describe the drug as having saved their marriage from drinking. Neither account appears in clinical literature.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measured change in turnout. 'They're sedating the workforce' moved from rhetoric to a labour grievance: a Columbus, Ohio warehouse local's NLRB and EEOC complaints over Steady Shift give the backlash its first institutional foothold. Because the MAHA wing funds the anhedonia study, any finding will arrive already partisan.

state.regulatory_posture: Split, and tightening at the edges. The FDA imposed a NAION class warning, ended personal-importation discretion for incretins and declined priority review for the AUD sNDA. HHS finalised a rule ending the 'adequate provision' pathway for broadcast DTC ads of chronic weight-management drugs, so 30-second TV spots disappeared in 2030. Meanwhile CMS made the Continuity Model mandatory and national. The administration is both the largest payer and the loudest critic.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Public programmes are now the default payer: the Medicare Continuity Model is national and mandatory for Part D sponsors (~3.8M obesity-only enrollees), 31 Medicaid states cover obesity at $245, and TrumpRx sells orals at $149. Nine states (led by Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana and Florida) bar incretin prescribing for weight in under-16s and require a pediatric specialist and a 6-month lifestyle programme for 16–17-year-olds.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare and 15 Medicaid waivers require ≥80% refill adherence and ≥5% loss at 6 months, with a 6-month lockout on lapse (adverse-event exemptions). About 1 in 4 large self-funded employers run BMI or adherence surcharges, typically $50–100/month, waived on connected-pen or refill proof. Some employers now use the same data for scheduling preference. Texas's surcharge ban still does not reach ERISA plans. Bills to extend it to scheduling have stalled in Ohio and Illinois.
state.workforce_or_military: Army and Air Force accession waivers for recruits who reach standards on a GLP-1 (≥6 months off-drug stability) continue. TRICARE active-duty coverage is unchanged. The NAION warning added a vision re-check to aviation waivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Jun 2029 Section 232 tariff of 50% on GLP-1 peptide API and finished injectables from countries without onshoring agreements, together with CBP seizures, shut most of the India–US personal-import channel. India filed a WTO consultation request. Lilly and Novo are exempt for onshored lines and partly exposed elsewhere. Canadian generics are still bought in person by border-state residents in small quantities, under informal tolerance.

events.event: Unsealed documents in the federal GLP-1 multidistrict litigation show Novo Nordisk's safety team proposed an adjudicated NAION analysis of pooled semaglutide trials in 2024 that management deferred; DOJ issues a civil investigative demand and Novo's head of global safety departs.

Commerce imposes a 50% Section 232 tariff on GLP-1 peptide ingredients and finished injectables from countries without US onshoring agreements, and FDA and CBP end enforcement discretion for personal importation of incretins; telehealth import prices roughly double and CBP reports 1.2M seized parcels by year-end.

Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, Florida and five other states enact laws barring weight-loss incretin prescriptions for children under 16; HHS finalises a rule that effectively ends 30-second TV ads for chronic weight-management drugs.

FDA adds a class warning for NAION, a sudden optic-nerve stroke, to every GLP-1 receptor agonist label including orals, tirzepatide and retatrutide, citing a roughly doubled risk and an absolute excess of 1–2 cases per 10,000 patient-years.

CMS makes the Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model mandatory for all Part D plans at the same $245/$50 terms, widens eligibility, adds retatrutide, and shortens the lapse lockout to six months; 31 states now cover obesity in Medicaid, making public programmes the largest payer of incretin prescriptions.

A Columbus, Ohio warehouse workers' local files NLRB and EEOC complaints against a national logistics firm's 'Steady Shift' rostering, which gives preferred schedules to employees whose connected pens show adherence to the company's weight programme.

open_tensions: Public programmes are now the default payer, and they pay on condition of proven adherence. About 7M obesity-only public enrollees are tracked by refill and weigh-in data, and employers have started using the same signal to schedule people. When US generics arrive in 2031–32, the $245 rate, the adherence conditions and the data pipelines will all be renegotiated at once.

The Novo documents and the NAION class warning have turned the safety ledger into a litigation map. MDL bellwethers begin in 2031, the hyposmia signal is unresolved in the US, and the Sentinel cycling study hints at a lean-mass ratchet in the ~34% of ever-users who cycle, many of them cycled by policy rather than choice.

Employers reward steadiness just as an alcohol indication is pending (decision 2031) and the first anhedonia study, funded by the drug's political critics, is under way. Any finding about reward blunting will land in a labour dispute and a partisan fight, not a clinic.

Nine states restrict minors' access while the adolescents already treated elsewhere approach their five-year mark. The 2029 import crackdown has left ~2.5M working-age regainers, too young for Medicare and too well paid for Medicaid, waiting for generics.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, with oral initial doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) at $149/month.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
Medicare pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay for covered obesity use, the rate set in the Nov 2025 deals.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.

prose.headline: The Government Is Now America's Biggest Buyer of Weight-Loss Drugs. It Pays for Your Pen, and It Checks Your Refills.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about 46 million American adults are on an incretin drug, slightly fewer than two years ago. The number barely moved, but who pays for it changed completely. For the first time, Washington pays for more of these prescriptions than employers do. Medicare's obesity programme stopped being a pilot in January and became mandatory for every Part D plan. It still pays $245 a month, the copay is still $50, and the programme still checks whether patients refill on time and lose five percent in six months. Nearly four million older Americans are enrolled, and thirty-one state Medicaid programmes now cover obesity on the same terms. Counting diabetics, public programmes pay for about four in ten fills.

The working-age middle lost ground. Employer weight-management coverage slid to 38 percent. In June 2029 a tariff on imported peptide ingredients, together with an end to the FDA's tolerance of personal importation, shut down most of the cheap Indian-generic trade that had kept six million people on the drug for $60 to $120 a month. Parcels were seized and prices doubled. About two and a half million people stopped, and in warehouse towns in Ohio and Texas their weight came back where the neighbours could see it. Brand cash prices rose as well: injectable semaglutide went to $249 on TrumpRx and retatrutide to $449. The daily pills stayed at $149, so nearly half of new patients now start on a pill.

Retatrutide, Lilly's triple agonist, is now ordinary. About four million people take it, Medicare covers it, and bariatric surgery volumes are down nearly a third from 2026. 'Reta face' is a recognised look, and strength gyms market themselves to people trying to keep their muscle.

The drug's reputation cracked in February 2029, when court documents showed that Novo Nordisk's own safety staff had proposed a careful analysis of sudden optic-nerve strokes and been told to wait. In November the FDA put a vision warning on every drug in the class. The absolute risk is small, a case or two per ten thousand patient-years, but the warning came with a story about a hidden document, and stories outlast numbers. Optometry chains now advertise annual 'GLP-1 eye checks'. Novo's head of safety is gone, the Justice Department is asking questions, and the first trials in the litigation are set for next year.

The administration is the drug's biggest buyer and its loudest critic. Nine states have barred weight-loss prescriptions for children under sixteen, and federal rules ended the thirty-second TV spots. The same HHS that pays for four million seniors' pens is funding the first study designed to measure whether the drugs dull pleasure, and the study's origin has already made its eventual result partisan.

In workplaces the drug's quiet has become an asset. Wellness vendors sell 'steadiness' metrics drawn from connected pens. A national logistics firm gave its best schedules to employees whose pens reported on time, and in June a Columbus warehouse union local filed federal complaints. Nobody in management says the drug makes workers calmer. They say adherent employees miss fewer shifts, which is true, and that people who keep their coverage keep their jobs, which is also true, and the two facts reinforce each other.

The counter-movement is angrier and still divided. Atlanta's fat-liberation organisers hold 'Full Table' Sundays, Texas congregations celebrate eating as grace, and wellness influencers quote the Novo documents. All of them cite the scandal, and they still disagree about almost everything else.

An off-label alcohol indication is pending and US generics are a year away. Snack volumes are down a few more points, spirits too. From the outside the country looks calm and well run, and each month it reports its refills to someone who is checking.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalczyk takes the Foundayo at 5:10 with coffee, standing at the counter in her robe. The bottle is the $149 one. Last spring her old pens from the Bangalore pharmacy stopped arriving. She got two emails saying 'customs hold', and then the site went dark.

She photographs the bottle for the Vireo app, because the app is what waives the seventy-five-dollar surcharge. A green check appears.

At the distribution centre on Alum Creek Drive the shift board shows her name under STEADY in blue. Pallets of protein bars come through the returns cage, short-dated. Marcus from the local is handing out flyers by the time clock, folded thirds about Steady Shift and the NLRB. She takes one and puts it in her vest pocket without reading it, because Marcus is still on nights.

At lunch she eats half a turkey sandwich and wraps the other half for Ray.

Ray is sixty-four. He lost forty pounds on the Indian pens and has found about twenty-five of them again. He has a calendar on the fridge with March circled, when he turns sixty-five and Medicare starts. At dinner he eats both halves of the sandwich and then a bowl of chili, slowly, watching the Guardians lose.

'You want some?'

'I'm good.'

She is good. That's the thing. She's mostly just good now.

In the bathroom she covers her left eye with her palm and reads the calendar through the doorway, then her right. The pharmacist gave her a little card about it. Both eyes work. She turns off the light.
